w: Tanzania's presidential State House began in 1865 as a residence for Majid bin Said, sultan of Zanzibar - wide verandahs overlooking the Indian Ocean, brass-studded doors, a pair of stone lions guarding the entrance. Inside, an Ethiopian shield gifted by Haile Selassie backs the president's chair.
_facts: Founded 1865 by Majid bin Said, Sultan of Zanzibar
Blends African and Arabian architecture, 33 acres of grounds
Brass-studded west doors with Coat of Arms replica, flanked by lion statues added 2001
Contains gifts from state visitors incl. Ethiopian shield from Haile Selassie

w: Tanzania's oldest museum started life in 1934 under British colonial governor Harold MacMichael and has since knitted itself into a nationwide consortium - the Village Museum, the Arusha Declaration Museum, even Julius Nyerere's memorial house all answer to it now. One museum, six outposts, a whole country's memory.
_facts: Founded 1934 as National Museum of Dar es Salaam by governor Harold MacMichael
Now a consortium of 7 museums incl. Village Museum, Arusha Declaration Museum, Nyerere Memorial Museum, Majimaji Memorial Museum

w: A bronze soldier levels his bayonet toward the harbour, at the reported centre of downtown Dar es Salaam - a 1927 memorial to the askari who fought Britain's WWI campaign in German East Africa. Cast in London by a sculptor signing himself 'Myrander,' its plaque credits Kipling: your sons will remember your name.
s: WWI memorial at downtown's dead centre
_facts: Unveiled 1927, honours King's African Rifles and Carrier Corps askari of WWI
Sculpted by James Alexander Stevenson (pseudonym 'Myrander'), exhibited at the Royal Academy first
Marks the reported exact centre of downtown Dar es Salaam
English inscription attributed to Rudyard Kipling

n: Saint Joseph's Cathedral, Dar es Salaam
w: German missionaries raised this Gothic cathedral on Sokoine Drive between 1897 and 1902, consecrating it in 1905 as the seat of the Dar es Salaam archdiocese. It still faces the harbour exactly as intended, stained glass glowing behind the altar - a slice of Bavarian ambition dropped on the Swahili coast.
s: German Gothic cathedral facing the harbour
_facts: Built 1897-1902 by Germans, consecrated 1905
Seat of the Dar es Salaam archdiocese
Notable stained-glass windows behind the altar
Faces the harbour on Sokoine Drive, near the White Fathers' House

w: Bavarian-style red-tiled roof, bright white walls, canopied windows facing the harbour - German missionaries built this Lutheran cathedral in 1898 and it has anchored the city-centre skyline ever since. One of Dar es Salaam's most photographed landmarks, and still a working cathedral for the local diocese.
_facts: Built 1898 by German missionaries in Bavarian style
Serves as cathedral for the local Lutheran diocese
Among the city's best-known landmarks and tourist attractions
Located city-centre, facing the harbour

w: A white obelisk in Mnazi Mmoja Park carries a replica of the Uhuru Torch at its tip, marking Tanzanian independence at the city's heart. Partly fenced, easy to walk past without a glance - and impossible to misread once you know what it is.
_facts: Also known as Uhuru Torch Monument
White obelisk topped with a replica of the Uhuru Torch
Located in Mnazi Mmoja Park, city centre, Mchafukoge ward

w: One of Dar es Salaam's oldest surviving buildings, built in 1866-67 for Sultan Majid bin Said next to his since-demolished palace, then restored and enlarged under German rule. Its carved Zanzibari door and coral-stone walls now front a heritage centre explaining how this city was actually built.
_facts: Built 1866-67 by Majid bin Said, Sultan of Zanzibar
Restored and enlarged under German rule
Carved Zanzibari-style wooden door, coral stone walls
Now houses DARCH, the Dar es Salaam Centre for Architectural Heritage

w: A protected, uninhabited island inside the Dar es Salaam Marine Reserve, a short boat ride from the city. No permanent residents - just endangered coconut crabs working the undergrowth - across roughly 14 square kilometres of reef, the wild edge of a fast-growing capital fenced off from development.
_facts: Protected uninhabited island, Dar es Salaam Marine Reserve, IUCN category II
Reserve measures around 14.2 sq km
Home to endangered coconut crabs
Neighbours Bongoyo and Pangavini islands

w: An Arab navigator named Ibn Majid logged this reef-fringed island back in 1470, and it has stayed largely untouched since - 19th-century ruins scattered across a protected marine reserve where coconut crabs, not people, hold the lease. Two islets, inner and outer, both off-limits to development.
s: Logged by an Arab navigator in 1470
_facts: First noted by Arab sailor Ibn Majid in 1470
Protected marine reserve, IUCN category II, ~4.6 sq km
Home to 19th-century ruins and endangered coconut crabs
Consists of inner and outer Sinda Island
